newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal transport strike strands commuters.
newsitem.headline: Nepal transport strike strands commuters.

text.p: A one-day strike by transport workers demanding higher wages and better working conditions paralysed public transport across Nepal on Wednesday and left commuters stranded, officials said.
Nepal has some 375,000 workers on more than 164,000 public transport vehicles, and buses, taxis, three-wheeled scooters and trucks all remained off the roads across the Himalayan kingdom.
The Independent Transport Workers' Association of Nepal (ITWAN) called the strike to demand better accident insurance coverage and the introduction of a minimum wage.

In Kathmandu, ITWAN leader Uddhav Khatri Chettri said four people were hurt when police charged a procession. A government spokesman denied any knowledge of the injuries and said police used "mild force" to prevent protesters from attacking a bus.
Jit Bahadur Karki, Secretary in the Ministry of Transport, told Reuters that most of the strikers' demands related to their employers who own the transport companies.
The workers want the government to introduce laws that would require employers to guarantee minimum service conditions.
Government officials in Kathmandu said they were willing to consider the workers' demands.
"If anything remains to be implemented...the government is prepared to see to their implementation as per the law," a government statement said.
But workers said the government lacked "serious concern" for their plight.
